scheme_name: Incentives for Meritorious Children (Students) of Workers (10th and 12th Class) (HBOCWWB)
description:
The Incentives for Meritorious Children of Workers scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India under the aegis of the Handloom and Handicrafts Board of the West Bengal Government.

This scheme was specifically introduced to provide financial assistance to the children of registered workers in the handloom and handicraft sectors.

The scheme was officially launched on 1st January 2019.

The primary objective of the scheme is to encourage academic excellence among the children of workers in these sectors.

The scheme aims to provide monetary incentives to meritorious students who have completed their 10th and 12th class examinations.

The financial assistance is intended to motivate students to pursue higher education and excel in their academic endeavors.

Under this scheme, students who secure at least 60% marks in their 10th or 12th class examinations are eligible for the incentive.

The amount of financial assistance provided under this scheme is ₹10,000 for students who pass the 10th class examination.

For students who pass the 12th class examination, the incentive amount is ₹15,000.

This financial support is intended to alleviate the financial burden on families and encourage students to continue their education.

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a child of a registered worker in the handloom or handicraft sector.

Students must also have completed their 10th or 12th class examinations from a recognized board.

There are no specific age limits mentioned for eligibility.

However, the income criteria state that the family income of the worker should not exceed ₹2 lakh per annum.

To apply for the scheme, the applicant must follow a specific process.

First, the applicant must obtain the application form from the official website or the local office of the Handloom and Handicrafts Board.

The application form must be filled out completely and accurately.

The applicant must attach necessary documents such as the worker's registration certificate.

Additionally, the applicant must provide proof of the student's academic performance.

This includes mark sheets of the 10th or 12th class examinations.

The completed application form along with the required documents must be submitted to the local office of the Handloom and Handicrafts Board.

The application process is designed to be straightforward to ensure that eligible students can access the benefits easily.

The timeline for application submission typically coincides with the announcement of examination results.

Applications are usually accepted within a month of the results being declared.

Disbursement of the incentive amount is generally processed within two months of the application submission.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Handloom and Handicrafts Board of West Bengal.

The board is responsible for overseeing the application process and ensuring that the incentives are disbursed to eligible students.

Contact details for the Handloom and Handicrafts Board can be found on their official website.

The board provides support and guidance for applicants throughout the process.

The scheme has been positively received by the community, with many families benefiting from the financial assistance.

Statistics indicate that in the first year of implementation, approximately 5,000 students received the incentive.

This number has steadily increased in subsequent years as awareness of the scheme has grown.

The government has allocated a budget of ₹5 crore for the scheme for the financial year 2023-2024.

This budget is intended to support the increasing number of applicants and ensure that all eligible students receive their incentives.

The scheme not only provides financial support but also aims to foster a culture of education among the families of workers.

By incentivizing academic performance, the scheme encourages students to strive for excellence.

The long-term goal of the scheme is to increase the literacy rate among the families of workers in the handloom and handicraft sectors.

This initiative aligns with the broader objectives of the government to promote education and skill development in India.

The scheme also serves to highlight the importance of education in improving the socio-economic status of families.

Through this initiative, the government aims to create a more educated workforce in the handloom and handicraft sectors.

The scheme is part of a larger framework of welfare initiatives aimed at supporting marginalized communities in India.

It reflects the government's commitment to empowering workers and their families through education.

In summary, the Incentives for Meritorious Children of Workers scheme is a targeted initiative designed to support the educational aspirations of children from the handloom and handicraft sectors.

With specific financial incentives for academic achievement, the scheme aims to foster a culture of learning and excellence.

The eligibility criteria are clearly defined, and the application process is streamlined to ensure accessibility.

The financial assistance provided is significant and aims to alleviate the economic pressures faced by families.

Overall, this scheme represents a crucial step towards enhancing educational opportunities for the children of workers in India.
